text: Every AI workflow this chapter covered used sanitized examples on purpose. A prompt to a third-party LLM is data leaving your control the moment you send it.
Real customer PII, API keys, connection strings, and unredacted production data never belong in a prompt to a hosted model — use synthetic or masked data instead.
An LLM's output reads persuasively whether or not it's right. A claim traced to a real log line or checked sample row beats any amount of fluent-sounding certainty.
Handing a task to an LLM doesn't transfer responsibility for the output — the engineer who ships it owns it.
Sanitize the input, verify the output, own the result. Next up: the cost and latency trade-offs of AI-augmented pipelines.
